book_paragraphs: Knowing that a company is a quality compounder is only half the battle. The other half is reading institutional footprints on the price-and-volume tape so you never buy an extended peak or hold a broken trend. On November 23, 2026, Coforge's tape confirmed that its Stage 2 uptrend remains firmly intact, even as short-term volatility tests weak hands.

On the verified November 23 NSE session, Coforge surged 2.66% to close at ₹2,142.30—just 1.63% shy of its ₹2,177.80 52-week high—on 4.44 million shares, or 1.51x its 20-day average volume. Over the prior week it gained 6.58%, lifting its 28-day relative strength to +2.66% and 63-day relative strength to +9.22% versus the Nifty 50. Two days later, the live TradingView snapshot captured a sharp 3.84% single-session pullback to ₹2,060.00, resetting daily RSI from 68.75 back down to a balanced 55.50.

That pullback is a textbook reminder of why we never chase above the buy zone. At ₹2,142.30, Coforge had stretched 8.10% above its rising 10-week EMA (₹1,981.72) and bumped directly into Pivot R1 resistance at ₹2,150.00. At ₹2,060.00, price sits right back inside the ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18 support shelf, just 3.95% above its 10-week EMA and 1.17% above its 20-day EMA (₹2,036.18).

Even more striking is the volatility compression. Bollinger bandwidth has tightened further from 10.76% in our prior dossier to just 7.96%—an unusually tight Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP) above rising 50-day (₹1,930.11) and 30-week (₹1,722.55) moving averages. Meanwhile, the broader Nifty 50 regime remains an Uptrend with narrow breadth (55.2% of 500 stocks above their 50-DMA, 3 distribution days), an environment where institutional capital concentrates into visible earnings leaders and upcoming MSCI Emerging Markets additions.

Because we now hold 41 shares in Zerodha, trend discipline becomes concrete risk management. As the 30-week SMA climbed ₹30 higher from ₹1,692.22 to ₹1,722.55, our upward-only stop-loss ratchet raises our hard structural stop from ₹1,659.40 to ₹1,685.64. We never widen a stop downward; we trail it up behind rising weekly institutional support.

Why does our 4-hour chart matter so much right now? Because weekly and daily trends tell you the primary direction, while the 4-hour chart tells you whether short-term sellers have finished unloading. On the November 25 pullback to ₹2,060.00, 4-hour RSI dipped to 49.47 and price slipped just below the 4-hour 20-period EMA at ₹2,063.13 while holding above the 4-hour 50-period SMA at ₹2,023.24. With no confirmed 4-hour upward turn yet, patience keeps you from catching a falling knife a few sessions before the November 30 MSCI Emerging Markets index rebalance.

Volume context reinforces that calm stance. Over the trailing 25 sessions, Coforge logged four distribution days against a Nifty 50 benchmark carrying three distribution days, while TheWrap places Coforge in the 85.1 relative strength percentile even though IT Services sector breadth sits at just 33.3%. In narrow markets, capital rewards leaders that hold their 20-day and 50-day shelves.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Alignment: 1W, 1D, and 4H Readout
paragraphs: Inspecting all three timeframes explains the exact tactical posture. On the Weekly (1W) chart, the trend is unambiguously bullish: 1W RSI stands at 65.15, price sits +19.59% above the rising 30-week SMA (₹1,722.55), and the 10-week EMA (₹1,981.72) slopes upward. On the Daily (1D) chart, price holds above the 20D EMA (₹2,036.18), 50D SMA (₹1,930.11), and 200D SMA (₹1,572.27), with a tight 7.96% Bollinger bandwidth.

The 4-Hour (4H) chart is where short-term caution lives. At ₹2,060.00, price dipped marginally below the 4H EMA20 (₹2,063.13) while holding above the 4H SMA50 (₹2,023.24), with 4H RSI at 49.47 and no confirmed upward turn yet. That tells us not to rush: let buyers defend the ₹1,982–₹2,036 band (10W EMA to 20D EMA) before adding shares.

book_subsections.title: Catalyst Tape: MSCI Nov 30 Rejig & Overhead Resistance
paragraphs: Volume expanded during the November 23 push to ₹2,142.30 (4.44M shares, 1.51x 20D average) as positioning built ahead of Coforge's November 30, 2026 addition to the MSCI Global Standard / Emerging Markets Index. Passive index inclusions frequently create elevated two-way volatility around the effective date—rallying into the window, followed by brief profit-taking before fundamentals reassert control.

Above the market, Pivot R1 sits at ₹2,150.00 (just below the ₹2,185.60 52-week high), followed by Pivot R2 at ₹2,255.00. On the downside, initial institutional demand rests at ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18, secondary structural support sits at Pivot S1 (₹1,851.80), and full Stage 2 invalidation is now raised to ₹1,685.64.
